paperTitle: O-Level English — Basic Band Practice 05: The Queue
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band (2026-08-14). Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Spec: ~250-word passage, high-frequency vocabulary, short sentences, 5 questions / 5 marks, 3 of them click-only. Q1-Q2 short answer (1-4 words), Q3 vocabulary in context, Q4 literal, Q5 feeling — all MCQ.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers. One or two words are enough.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
My father does not like sweet things. He does not eat cake. He says fruit is enough.

Paragraph 2
So I did not understand why he stood in the durian queue for fifty minutes on a Saturday afternoon in June.

Paragraph 3
The queue went past two shops. The floor was wet. Flies came and went. My father did not move out of the line even once.

Paragraph 4
When we reached the front, he pointed at one durian and asked the man to open it. He smelled it, nodded, and paid.

Paragraph 5
He did not eat any of it. Not one seed. He carried the box on the bus with both hands, on his lap, all the way to Toa Payoh.

Paragraph 6
My grandmother is eighty-one. She cannot walk far now, and she has not been to a durian stall in three years.

Paragraph 7
When we opened the box in her flat, she laughed. She ate two seeds and then a third. My father sat and watched her eat.

Paragraph 8
On the bus home I asked him why he queued so long for something he does not even like.

Paragraph 9
'She used to queue,' he said. 'For me.'

questions.stem: Q1. From Paragraph 2, how long did the father stand in the queue? [1]
Q2. From Paragraph 6, how old is the grandmother? [1]

questions.stem: Q3. In Paragraph 3, the father 'did not move out of the line even once'. What does this show? [1]

options.text: He was afraid of the flies.
He was determined to wait for the durian.
He could not find another shop.
He was too tired to walk away.

questions.stem: Q4. How did the father carry the durian on the bus? [1]

options.text: In a bag on the floor.
He asked the writer to hold it.
With both hands, on his lap.
He left it at the durian stall.

questions.stem: Q5. What does the father's answer in Paragraph 9 tell us? [1]

options.text: He is repaying his mother's kindness from long ago.
He has started to enjoy durian.
He wants the writer to queue next time.
His mother had asked him to buy it.
